questions.question: When a school bus has flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Stop at least 10 feet away from the bus.
Pass if children have exited the bus.
Stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a barrier.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at least 10 feet away from the bus.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop at least 10 feet away. The only exception is if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have difficulty staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired while driving, stop driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass this sign, you are going the wrong way. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to make night driving safer for you and other drivers.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after rain starts.
Give yourself more space when stopping.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain begins. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from slipping.

questions.question: If a police officer requires you to take a blood, breath, or urine test, you:

options.text: May choose which test you prefer.
Must take the test or your license will be suspended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must take the test or your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: If police arrest you for driving under the influence and you refuse a chemical test, your license will be suspended for one year. This suspension stays in place even if you are found not guilty.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
Decreases the number of driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more errors.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect driving compared to other things?

options.text: The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol affect driving safety in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: You are stopped at a stop sign but cannot see cross traffic clearly. What should you do?

options.text: Lower your windows, listen for traffic, then go.
Move forward slowly, look for traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly, look for traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign where you cannot see cross traffic, yield to pedestrians. Slowly move forward past the stop line until you can see clearly. Check for traffic and pedestrians. Go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey these signals. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic at that intersection.

questions.question: Which of these things put distracted drivers at greater crash risk?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) or any audio device (radio or CD player) can distract you while driving and increases crash risk.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Slow down more on slippery roads than you would in normal conditions.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Turn with a smaller radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: You see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.
